# Optimizing Page Load Performance with Native HTML Lazy Loading

**Source:** https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dax66INgK3F/ · **Type:** Reel · **Author:** Toushif Ahmed · **Saved:** 2026-10-06

**Why I saved it:** Web dev img loading tip

## Summary

Browsers by default download all page images simultaneously upon load, causing unnecessary network overhead and degrading Core Web Vitals. Adding the native HTML attribute loading="lazy" to image elements defers offscreen downloads until users scroll near them.

## Transcript and on-screen text

Have you ever noticed this? When a website has lots of images and you open or reload the page, it can take longer to load. That's because the browser starts downloading every image at once, even the ones you can't see yet. This creates unnecessary network requests, affects page performance, and can hurt your Core Web Vitals. The solution is surprisingly simple: just add one HTML attribute, loading="lazy". And if I add it to my HTML, here's what happens. Now the browser only loads the images that are visible on the screen. As the user scrolls, the remaining images load automatically. One small HTML attribute can make your website much smarter. Follow for more web development tips.

## Caption

Most Developers Forget This HTML Attribute!

Did you know you can improve your website's performance with just one HTML attribute? 

Instead of downloading every image at once, use loading="lazy" to load images only when they're about to appear on the screen. This reduces unnecessary network requests and helps improve page performance, especially on image-heavy websites.

💡 A small HTML attribute can make a big difference.
